Testimony of Senate President Mattie Daughtry in support of LD 954, "An Act to Amend the Law Governing the Membership of the Government
Oversight Committee" Presented to the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
March 26, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government, my name is Mattie Daughtry. I serve as President of the Maine Senate and proudly represent Senate District 23 in the Legislature, which includes Brunswick, Freeport, Harpswell, Pownal, Chebeague Island, and part of Yarmouth. I am here to testify in support of LD 954, "An Act to Amend the Law Governing the Membership of the Government Oversight Committee."
This bill, as the title suggests, simply removes requirements related to the membership of the Government Oversight Committee, or GOC. In the 131st Legislature, we changed the law regarding membership to specify and favor broad representation from other committee membership. The intent of this bill was good, the goal to balance committee membership is admirable. This change was well intentioned and I appreciate the effort to make sure GOC has the right membership to carry out its important mission. Before that change, the membership of the committee and the selection of chairs are established by joint rule of the Legislature. To me, that joint rule is what we should return to as one Legislature should not tie the hands of the next. And there is good reason for that.
It is important that we leave this to Presiding Officers. I am not here because I want to change the Committee's membership in the 132nd Legislature, but because I don't believe legislative leaders hands to be tied when considering who is best to serve. I don't want any other Presiding Officer's hands to be tied in the future.
When considering who to place on the Government Oversight Committee, we should appoint a members who want to be on the Committee, who understand that there will be a diverse range of issues to consider and is eager to dive into them. We should appoint members who understand why the GOC is important and is aligned with the values behind the push for accountability in government. Appointment decisions should be made entirely on these considerations, without also having to consider the priorities of a previous Legislature.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to take questions.

Testimony of Senator Nicole Grohoski
LD 954, "An Act to Amend the Law Governing the Membership of the
Government Oversight Committee"

Before the Committee on State and Local Government 26 March 2025

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing
Committee on State and Local Government, my name is Nicole Grohoski, and I proudly
represent Senate District 7, which includes 22 coastal communities in Downeast Maine. Thank
you for the opportunity to testify on LD 954, "An Act to Amend the Law Governing the
Membership of the Government Oversight Committee."

I am testifying neither for nor against this bill in order to provide context for the origin of the membership requirements for the Government Oversight Committee (GOC) that this bill seeks to
eliminate.
As a reminder, the GOC has 12 members: 3 Senate Democrats, 3 Senate Republicans, 3 House Democrats, and 3 House Republicans. The law currently requires GOC to have 1 member who is
also on the Taxation Committee (TAX) and one member who is also on the Housing and Economic Development Committee (HED). Further, it requires that no 2 members of the committee may serve on the same policy committee and be in the same political party.
These requirements were established by LD 849 in the 131st Legislature: "An Act to Implement
the Recommendations of the Working Group to Review the Process for Ongoing Review of Tax Expenditures by the Legislature." I was not part of the working group` nor have I done a deep dive on its proceedings, but this bill came before the Taxation Committee, which I co-chair.
The working group originally recommended that 2 members of GOC also serve on TAX and 1 on HED. TAX felt that our policy area did not need that level of representation on GOC to serve
as an effective bridge between the committees for the tax expenditure review process. However,
we felt that having a broad range of policy committee expertise on GOC could help inform the

This bill allows the Legislature to have an important conversation about how to best "staff" the
Government Oversight Committee, which has a significant role to play in the Legislature's
oversight of the Executive Branch. I'm disappointed that this bill proposes to remove the
requirement to have a diversity of committee expertise on GOC before we get to see how
effective the idea was.
The decision to remove membership requirements for one TAX and one HED member should be considered in conjunction with LD 136, "An Act to Transfer the Responsibility for Tax
Expenditure Review from the Government Oversight Committee to the Joint Standing
Committee on Taxation." If that bill is passed, it makes sense to remove the related GOC
membership requirements. If it is not passed, then I think it would be prudent to at least retain
that part of statute. In my experience on TAX, the tax expenditure review process hand-off
between GOC and TAX has not been very effective, but we hope that with members now
bridging both committees, we might improve it.
Thank you for your time and consideration of my testimony. I would be happy to answer any
questions.
